h2: NDT training near Detroit: Monroe County Community College, welding-program inspection courses and online theory compared
html:
NDT training near Detroit: Monroe County Community College, welding-program inspection courses and online theory compared

Southeast Michigan does have college NDT coursework, though not in Detroit itself. Monroe County Community College, south of the city, offers NDT certificates, and Washtenaw Community College in Ann Arbor builds inspection and testing into its welding programs. Add employer training at automotive suppliers, refiners and power plants, plus online theory with a practical at work, and a Detroit candidate has four routes to compare.

Who offers NDT training around Detroit?

  • Monroe County Community College, Monroe. Basic and advanced NDT certificates covering the five major methods: visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and radiographic testing. The college says the coursework is set in line with ASNT's SNT-TC-1A and that the certificates are relevant to its welding and nuclear technology associate degrees. The main campus is in Monroe, about 40 miles south of downtown, with a second center in Temperance.
  • Washtenaw Community College, Ann Arbor. Welding students take an inspection and testing course covering visual inspection to AWS D1.1, penetrant, magnetic particle, radiography and ultrasonic angle-beam and phased array work, alongside destructive tests. The instructor told the AWS magazine Inspection Trends in 2024 that the aim is welders who can troubleshoot their own work rather than inspectors.
  • Employer training. Automotive and casting suppliers, the refinery in southwest Detroit, downriver steel operations and nuclear and fossil plants train their own technicians under written practices.
  • ASNT Detroit Section. ASNT lists a Detroit Section, and its meetings connect candidates with working Level IIIs.

Certificate, welding course or method training?

The three are easy to confuse. A Monroe certificate is NDT training across several methods, a solid base for someone starting from scratch. A Washtenaw inspection course makes a welder better at judging welds, which is valuable, but it was designed for welders rather than as a path to Level II. Method training is narrower still: one method, taken to the level your job needs, with the hours recorded for your employer's written practice. Pick the one that matches the step you are on.

Detroit-area manufacturers add a further layer. Production NDT on castings, forgings and welded assemblies is usually done to the customer's material specification, so a supplier's written practice may ask for more formal hours or a method the college certificate does not take to Level II. Ask the employer's Level III which specification governs before you choose a course.

Which route fits you?

Starting pointRoute in southeast MichiganCaution
Starting from zeroMCCC's basic, then advanced, certificateYou still need an employer to certify you
Welder who wants to inspectWashtenaw's inspection course, then NDT method theoryA welding course does not log NDT hours
Technician adding a method or levelOnline method theory, then the practical and exams at your employerAsk your Level III how outside hours count
Supplier certifying its teamOn-site training and exams run by a Level IIIMatch scope to customer specifications

Questions to ask any Detroit-area NDT provider

  • Which methods and levels, and how many hours each?
  • Will you inspect castings, forgings or welds with real flaws?
  • Who certifies you? Your employer, under its written practice.
  • Can you reach a Level III with questions?

Where Atlantis fits for Detroit candidates and employers

Atlantis covers the method-training step without a drive to Monroe or Ann Arbor. You study online on the Atlantis portal at your own pace, put questions to an ASNT Level III, and begin whenever you enroll. Practice in the Practical NDT simulator comes before the hands-on practical and practical exam at your employer's facility, run under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A; your employer certifies you. Detroit's casting, forging and spot-weld work calls for ultrasonic testing training, magnetic particle testing training and penetrant testing training; try the free practice tests to see where you stand.

Tier suppliers and casting plants around Detroit that certify their own people can have the training run on-site, using their parts and instruments, with a Level III administering exams and keeping the qualification records in order for customer and registrar audits.

A Monroe certificate holder who lands a job can carry one method to Level II online while logging experience at work. Weld inspectors can add the six-day CWI exam prep for Detroit. Nearby pages: Michigan, Toledo and Grand Rapids.
